correction_2026_10_08: THE SOURCE'S OWN QUALIFIER IS KEPT. Two rows here moved from the bare leaf to the published qualified name, and both moved because the SOURCE spells the owner: `C.create()` and `C.total` were emitted as `create` and `total`. The analyzer now writes a qualified target only when it can point at the declaration it names — the owner must be a type the file publishes AND must declare the member (or the project index must say so) — so this is a sharpening, not a guess. Verified by re-running this fixture: `other.count` (a parameter receiver, type unread) is still the bare `count`, which is the control that the rewrite is not blanket-qualifying every member read.
correction_2026_10_10: THE RECEIVER-TYPE SPELLING, and the DT-A CONVENTION IT DELIBERATELY SUPERSEDES. DT-A pinned 'an unknown cross-file `X.y()` stays a leaf call', because the leaf was the only thing the analyzer could name; the census then priced the alternative against the gate's own key space (calls: +12,845 ambiguous rows resolve, 2,748 resolved rows stop being resolvable; uses: +29,638 and 2,564 — four repositories, dart-sdk still running) and the decision was made to spell: a bare member whose receiver's type name the run can NAME (`X.y()`, `a?.bump()` and a local with an explicit type alike) now publishes `<Type>.<member>` and carries `baseBeyondRunScope: <Type>`, the declared cause that says the run could not look the owner up. The claim can never raise a resolution — the gate reads it only where the target names nothing — so the four rows below that changed are a SHARPENING plus an honest bucket-3 reason, not an exemption. What did NOT change is the control that matters: `other.count` (a parameter whose type this pass does not read) is still the bare `count` with `receiverTypeUnknown`, which is the pin that the spelling is not blanket-qualifying every member read. THE UN-DEDUP is recorded here too: `uses useAll -> A.count` is a NEW row, because in the pre-fix state it collided on (source, type, target) with the untyped `count` read and only one of the two survived; naming the owner makes them two different edges, and the fixture now pins both.
rationale: First Dart review wave: DT-A named construction wins over dangling leaf calls (in-file knowledge; statics and cross-file X.y() stay calls), DT-B heritage aliases resolve (on/with), DT-C redirect targets resolve, DT-D super()/this() initializer redirections instantiate, DT-F member reads (qualified selectors, cascade getters, subscript bases, interpolation). Every pin probe-verified against both the analyzer and the deriveDartEdges oracle before pinning; lanes confirm the pair agrees on corpora.
